acting_agent.description: The verified token holder. Null for a token minted for a tool call.
acting_agent.title: Acting Agent

action_id.description: The audit row for this decision. Required by the token exchange. Null only when the decision could not be recorded.
action_id.title: Action Id

guarantee.description: Echoed from the request and written to the audit row. Null only on a response rendered before the request was parsed.

hop.description: Derived from the verified act chain
hop.title: Hop

message.description: Human-readable detail; never the machine contract
message.title: Message

privileged.description: The target is privileged in the session's pinned policy.
privileged.title: Privileged

recorded.description: The audit row was committed before this response was sent.
recorded.title: Recorded

step_up.description: Present only on a RECOVERABLE deny with step-up enabled: the challenge to put to the consenting human. A non-recoverable deny never carries one, so a client cannot offer a prompt for something that can never be granted (FR-024).

taint.description: The EFFECTIVE taint the decision was made under, not an echo of the request.

taint_source.description: The target that introduced the taint into this context.
taint_source.title: Taint Source

transaction_required.description: privileged AND transaction tokens enabled: mint POST /v1/token/transaction before calling the resource.
transaction_required.title: Transaction Required

enforced.description: Reported by the enforcement point: will it act on a deny, or is it in observe mode? An allow is always recorded as enforced, since it is forwarded either way — so `enforced=false` means exactly 'would have been blocked'. NEVER an input to the decision itself: the PDP is mode-blind, which is what makes the observe-mode report a trustworthy prediction of enforcement.
enforced.title: Enforced

guarantee.description: How strong the enforcement at this point actually is. Reported by the enforcement point, exactly like `enforced`, and NEVER an input to the decision. **Deliberately no default**: a PEP that omits it gets a 422, which is how FR-018 ('refuse to emit a decision whose guarantee level cannot be determined') is enforced by the schema rather than by a runtime branch some path could miss.

taint.description: Agent-reported label. ADDITIVE ONLY: it can raise the effective taint the decision uses, never lower it (Phase 4). The control plane derives the rest.

at_hop.description: The first hop whose link could not be established
at_hop.title: At Hop

ChainRead.description: One recorded action's full delegation path, from one row plus its session.
ChainRead.title: ChainRead

data_classes.description: Subset of the pinned policy's data classes to consent to. Omit for all of them. Every entry must be declared by some agent in the compiled scope.
data_classes.title: Data Classes

ConsentRead.description: What the integrator gets back. ``root_grant`` is the hop-1 token.
ConsentRead.title: ConsentRead

Guarantee.description:
Strongest to weakest. The order of declaration is not the contract — ``STRENGTH``
is — but keeping them aligned makes the file readable.
Guarantee.title: Guarantee

RootConsent.description: The human at the start of every chain, and what they approved.
RootConsent.title: RootConsent

StepUpChallenge.description:
The challenge handed back on a recoverable deny.

Defined here rather than in ``app.schemas.stepup`` to keep ``AuthorizeDecision``'s
imports acyclic: the step-up schemas import the deny vocabulary from this module.

challenge_id.description: Single use. Only its SHA-256 is ever stored.
challenge_id.title: Challenge Id

StepUpChallenge.title: StepUpChallenge

TaintPolicyDecl.description:
Phase 4 provenance policy for THIS agent (contracts/taint.md §2).

``trusted_sources``: globs over target refs whose results are trusted_internal for this
agent. ``None`` means "my declared downstream agents, nothing else" — materialized by the
compiler so the runtime never has to know the default. ``block_tainted_into``: targets a
tainted context may not call; ``"privileged"`` means every privileged tool, a glob matches
the target ref or the call's data class.
TaintPolicyDecl.title: TaintPolicyDecl

TransactionFingerprint.description:
The FR-042 fingerprint of a privileged call's transaction token: the binding digest
and lifetime, never the token. Joined from ``transaction_tokens`` on ``action_id``.
TransactionFingerprint.title: TransactionFingerprint

params.description: The call's parameters, a JSON object. Bound per contracts/canonicalization.md.
params.title: Params

binding.description: RFC 6901 pointers applied, or null for the whole body
binding.title: Binding

params_hash.description: base64url SHA-256 of the canonical binding document
params_hash.title: Params Hash

bearerAuth.description: The admin bearer token (AGENTIC_AUTH_ADMIN_TOKEN in a local dev setup) for most routes, or the audit-reader token for /v1/audit/*. GET /.well-known/jwks.json needs no token at all.

schema.title: Response Get Jwks  Well Known Jwks Json Get

post.description:
Idempotent. Cuts off the anchor and every hop that would extend this agent's
authority — checked at the next authorize and exchange, and by offline verifiers within
their freshness window.

get.description: The full delegation chain for one recorded action, back to the consenting human.
Filtered decision history, newest first, stable under concurrent appends.

The same material as ``/agents/{id}/identity``, addressed by the agent's name.

A resource server knows the agents it expects by name and holds only an identity-reader
token, which cannot list agents (that listing is admin-only) — so it bootstraps through
this route instead.

servers.description: Local control plane — see the Get Started tutorial
